signals.title: Every response carries X-Instance-ID, a v4 UUID naming the Rocket.Chat server instance

headers.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self' https://cdn.zapier.com; connect-src *; font-src 'self' https://cdn.zapier.com data:; frame-src *; img-src * data: blob:; media-src * data:; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-eval' 'sha256-jqxtvDkBbRAl9Hpqv68WdNOieepg8tJSYu1xIy7zT34=' 'sha256-aui5xYk3Lu1dQcnsPlNZI+qDTdfzdUv3fzsw80VLJgw=' https://cdn.zapier.com https://zapier.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://cdn.zapier.com

signals.evidence: X-Instance-Id: e287198e-5576-4f77-898f-18ea23e4d9e4
signals.notes: A header Rocket.Chat invented: the base middleware instanceIdHeader (registered in apps/meteor/server/lib/http/baseMiddlewares.ts:5) sets it on every response, REST, pages, files and errors alike (all 83 responses captured for this stage carry it), to InstanceStatus.id(), which is randomUUID() per process (packages/instance-status/src/index.ts:9). The value changes on every restart and differs per instance in a cluster, so match its shape, never its value. Breaks only if a reverse proxy or CDN strips unknown response headers. The app emits it as X-Instance-ID; the lab's Traefik rewrote the name to the canonical X-Instance-Id, and header names are case-insensitive. Another application could choose the same header name, so pair it with FP-002 when certainty matters. Did not match either control: a bare nginx:1.27-alpine container and Mailpit v1.31.4 (an unrelated Go web app with a single-page UI), both replayed with the same request.

signals.notes: The page CSP is built by the securityHeaders base middleware: the first hash is of window.close() for the CAS login popup, the second of the inline script in the Livechat demo page (cors.ts:78-81), followed by the hard-coded Zapier hosts. Present on every captured response except the /livechat page (FP-026) while Enable_CSP is on, the shipped default (apps/meteor/server/settings/general.ts:95). Breaks if an admin turns Enable_CSP off, or a proxy replaces the CSP with its own. CDN_PREFIX and Extra_CSP_Domains add hosts around the hashes but do not move them apart. Did not match either control: a bare nginx:1.27-alpine container and Mailpit v1.31.4 (an unrelated Go web app with a single-page UI), both replayed with the same request.

The regex is anchored and back-references the issuer, so metadata that adds any field (an OIDC provider's jwks_uri, a scopes_supported list) or orders them differently does not match. Breaks if Site_Url carries a path (the document then moves to /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/<path>, metadata.ts:12-15). signals.notes: Rocket.Chat keeps sessions in localStorage and authenticates REST by header, so a default install sets no cookie on any anonymous response (none of the 83 responses captured for this stage set one). The only server-side Set-Cookie is cache_version, sent with Clear-Site-Data on static files only when an admin fills Troubleshoot_Force_Caching_Version (cors.ts:132-135); rc_uid and rc_token are written by the browser after login (apps/meteor/client/views/root/hooks/loggedIn/useStoreCookiesOnLogin.ts:14-15). The absence separates it from stacks that issue a session or CSRF cookie on first contact (PHP, Django, Rails); the meta literal ties the absence to Rocket.Chat. Breaks behind a proxy or load balancer that adds a stickiness cookie. Did not match either control: a bare nginx:1.27-alpine container and Mailpit v1.31.4 (an unrelated Go web app with a single-page UI), both replayed with the same request. On both controls the absent Set-Cookie part held too; the meta literal is what makes the signal specific.

Since 9.1 Rocket.Chat answers it from its own HTTP server, mimicking SockJS, and serves only the websocket transport (changeset own-http-server). This is the realtime DDP surface where the anonymous method and stream findings sit. Breaks behind proxies that route /sockjs elsewhere. Did not match either control: a bare nginx:1.27-alpine container and Mailpit v1.31.4 (an unrelated Go web app with a single-page UI), both replayed with the same request.

negative_signals.note: Not served: falls through to the page shell (200 text/html, same bytes as /). A 200 here is not a sitemap; scanners that treat 200 as presence get false positives on Rocket.Chat.
No security.txt is shipped; the path falls through to the page shell with 200 text/html.
Rocket.Chat's OAuth2 provider is not an OpenID provider: no OIDC discovery document, only the RFC 8414 one (FP-009); the path falls through to the page shell. GitLab and Keycloak serve JSON here.
The PWA manifest lives at /images/manifest.json (FP-021); /manifest.json falls through to the page shell.

Without the page's hash the runtime config is an empty 404 (apps/meteor/server/lib/cors/cors.ts:140-147). Meteor's own webapp package serves it at this URL with no hash check (programs/server/packages/webapp.js:641-645 in the shipped bundle), so a stock Meteor app answers 200 here. Separates Rocket.Chat from other Meteor apps.
Mattermost's health endpoint does not exist: plain-text 404 from the REST router, with Rocket.Chat's Access-Control-Allow-Headers. Separates it from Mattermost.
Zulip's server_settings endpoint does not exist (plain-text 404). Separates it from Zulip.

The SockJS xhr transport is not served (empty 404, apps/meteor/server/lib/realtime/routes.ts:24). The changeset own-http-server records that from 9.1 only the websocket transport is served and /sockjs xhr and polling answer 404, as in microservices deployments; because microservices deployments of older versions behave the same way, this is not used as a version signal.

403 with an empty body, not the icon: /assets/<key>.<ext> serves the admin-managed assets and the favicon key only allows svg (apps/meteor/server/lib/media/assets/assets.ts:424-427). The .ico asset is /assets/favicon_ico.ico; /favicon.ico is the static file (FP-003).

notes:
How these were observed. Every signal was fetched without credentials from the lab at http://127.0.0.1:39649 on 2026-11-24, through the vendor-documented Traefik reverse proxy in front of the app and through this session's egress proxy. Fetching the same paths from inside the lab, straight from the app container, showed that the two hops change only two things: Traefik rewrites header names to their canonical case (the app sends X-Instance-ID, the file shows X-Instance-Id; matchers compare names case-insensitively) and the egress proxy adds Connection: close. Each response.headers map is the full map as received here, those two included. blue_spider.fingerprints.check() replayed all 33 signals from this host and, separately, from inside the lab with the same code: 33 of 33 matched both times. Query strings are written into request.path because the replay tool appends nothing, so request.params is always empty. The reproduce lines take the target from $BASE and default to the lab.

Controls. Every signal was replayed against a bare nginx:1.27-alpine container started for this stage (bluespiderlab_rocket.chat_control on 127.0.0.1:39650, run on 0.05 CPU lent by the idle mail sink so the stack stayed inside its 3.0-CPU budget, then removed, with the mail sink's share restored) and against Mailpit v1.31.4, an unrelated Go web application already in the lab. Neither control matched any signal: 0 of 33 each, and check() reported matched_control 0. Where the generic half of a combined matcher did hold on a control, that signal's notes say so.

What masks or moves these signals in a real deployment. A reverse proxy or CDN may strip X-Instance-ID (FP-001), replace the CSP (FP-002), answer /favicon.ico itself (FP-003), add a stickiness cookie (FP-015), or block /api/docs, /livez, /_matrix or /livechat. A Site_Url with a path (https://host/chat) moves every path under that prefix, and moves the OAuth metadata to /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/chat. CDN_PREFIX moves /bundle/ and the script URLs to the CDN host; the regexes allow a host there. These admin settings each turn one signal off: Enable_CSP (FP-002), uploaded favicon assets (FP-004, FP-005, FP-006; FP-003 survives), Accounts_Password_Policy_Enabled (FP-010), API_Enable_Shields (FP-027), Accounts_AvatarExternalProviderUrl (FP-012), Robot_Instructions_File_Content (FP-033), API_Enable_CORS (FP-029), MCP_Enabled with its licence (FP-017), and the federation licence with Federation_Service_Enabled (FP-018). Site_Name changes the page title, which is why no signal matches the title.

Version. The exact build comes from /meteor_runtime_config.js (FP-030: git commit 9f3d6c8c48911e32ed6c2ce36befd431faa71190 and Meteor 3.5.2), which needs the per-deployment hash read from / first. Without it, /api/info gives major.minor (FP-011: 9.1, so >=9.1.0-develop and <9.2.0-develop), the Vite client under /bundle/ gives >=9.1.0-develop (FP-014), and four signals each set a 9.0 floor: OpenAPI 3.1 (FP-008), the RFC 8414 metadata (FP-009) and the MCP 404 (FP-017) from 9.0.0-rc.0, and the short 401 body (FP-016) from any 9.0.0 build, develop included. The ranges use Rocket.Chat's own tag scheme, where -develop is the lowest pre-release of a version. Only this one build could be observed, so every bound comes from the in-repo changelog, changesets and code at this commit, and nothing bounds the version from above except the major.minor of /api/info.

Not tested, and why. Other releases (the lab holds one build). HTTPS: the lab is plain HTTP per its manifest, so no TLS or HSTS signal is recorded, and none would describe the product. A microservices deployment, where a separate ddp-streamer serves DDP. Licensed (EE) workspaces with MCP or Matrix federation on. Workspaces served under a path prefix. A non-English server language, which changes the shield label (FP-027).

Candidates dropped. Generic or framework defaults: X-Powered-By: Express (sent only on Meteor-served responses), /health ({"status":"ok"}), the stock swagger-ui-express page at /api-docs/, the plain-text 404 of /api on its own, /websocket without an upgrade (SockJS's own 400 text), /oauth/token and /oauth/userinfo (OAuth library messages, rate limited), and /hooks/<id>/<token> with made-up values, which answers a bare 500 Internal Server Error: generic, and a probe that makes the server log an error is not one a fingerprint should send. Routes that 404 or 400 in a default install, so they fingerprint nothing: /file-decrypt/ (a 404 stub), /custom-sounds/<missing>, /file-upload/<missing>, /data-export/<missing>, /video-conference/rnnoise/<missing>, /api/apps/public/<missing>, /_saml/* (licensed), /i18n/<unknown language> (400), and /api/v1/mcp, whose JSON-RPC 'MCP endpoint is disabled' duplicates FP-017. Per-build or per-deployment values: the Meteor appId in the runtime config (generated at build time; the repository has no .meteor/.id), the supportedVersions token's timestamp (the newest of the build, licence and cloud copies), the main Meteor bundle /<sha1>.js?meteor_js_resource=true (named per build, and larger than the 512 KB the replay tool reads), and /i18n/en.json (532 KB). /readyz was not used as a signal because each call resets its event-loop histogram.

Passed on for the reviewer: one route was left out because it has a side effect, and it discloses data. GET /requestSeats (and /links/manage-subscription) answers anonymous callers with a 302 to https://go.rocket.chat/i/contact-sales carrying the workspace's active user count, plus its workspaceId and the setup wizard's Industry, Country and Size when those are set (apps/meteor/ee/server/requestSeatsRoute.ts:19-33, apps/meteor/ee/server/lib/license/getSeatsRequestLink.ts:6-30). Every call also increments a seat-request counter (requestSeatsRoute.ts:30, apps/meteor/server/services/analytics/service.ts:9-11). This stage reached that handler five times while classifying routes, and the lab's counter now reads 5; the statistics job resets it to 0 (apps/meteor/server/lib/statistics/lib/statistics.ts:471). Apart from that counter, and one early /readyz call that reset that probe's event-loop histogram as every orchestrator poll does, nothing in the lab was changed. No earlier stage recorded this disclosure in report.json.

No signal sends or needs a credential. Every signal is a GET except FP-029, an OPTIONS preflight; negative_signals include one POST, a SockJS transport handshake. No signal is an attack or a probe for a weakness.
